findings.summary: Sign-in continuation now accepts and consumes the invitation automatically, which skips the explicit ConsentPanel accept step and removes the guarantee that a validated invitation is preserved unconsumed until the invitee consents.
findings.evidence:
- Login continuation preserves a validated invitation without consuming it
+ Login continuation from an invitation accepts it for the invitee once sign-in succeeds, so they land on the new connection

findings.summary: ConsentPanel's new description limits it to invitees who were already signed in, which contradicts its unchanged cardinality of 'exactly one after validation' (validation also happens on the sign-in path).
findings.evidence:
cardinality: exactly one after validation
+ description: Shown to invitees who open the invitation while already signed in

findings.summary: The auto-accept effect specifies no failure handling for self-connection, block, expiry or replay that only becomes known after sign-in, even though the consent criterion requires the fixture to cover those cases for acceptance at sign-in.
findings.evidence: failure: [Provider unavailable shows the shared ErrorSummary] vs claim: "Invite fixture covers acceptance, including acceptance at sign-in, expiry, replay, self-connection, block and simultaneous redemption"
